title: Further props: middle knowledge, grace for all who will use the means, and man discerning himself against Paul and Luther
pass_a_gloss: So it is supposed that faith can be foreknown in these & those, antecedently to the decree concerning the giving of the grace of faith — on which matter in the Controversy on Middle Knowledge, with the Pontificals IX, with the Remonstrants XII. So they suppose that God wills to work in all this grace which is most special of the elect, of believers: So, that the same is destined in kind to those whom God foresees as going to use the means granted them, and not going to spurn grace, by themselves or through the greater ones, &c. Whence it seems to follow that a human being discerns himself, against Paul, & that in the human being there is a dispositive cause unto grace, or prior dispositions unto faith, against Luther's constant doctrine, in the Books On the Bondage of the Will, On the Origin of Faith, & the Preface to the Epistle to the Romans, &c.
pass_b_english: So it is supposed that faith can be foreknown in these and those before the decree to give the grace of faith — on which see the Controversy on Middle Knowledge, with the Pontificals IX and with the Remonstrants XII.

So they suppose that God wills to work in everyone this grace which is most special to the elect, to believers; and that the same grace is destined, as to its kind, to those whom God foresees will use the means granted them and will not spurn grace, by themselves or through their greater ones, and so on.

From this it seems to follow that a human being discerns himself — against Paul — and that in the human being there is a dispositive cause toward grace, or prior dispositions toward faith — against Luther's steady teaching in On the Bondage of the Will, On the Origin of Faith, and the Preface to the Epistle to the Romans, and elsewhere.
source_text: Ità supponitur, præsciri posse in his & illis fidem, antecedenter ad decretum de dandâ gratiâ fidei, quâ de re in Controv. de Scientia Media, cum Pontific. IX. cum Remonstr. XII. Ità supponunt, hanc gratiam quæ specialissima est electorum, credentium, velle Deum in omnibus operari: Ità, destinari eandem in specie, iis quos prævidet Deus usuros mediis sibi concessis, nec spreturos gratiam, per se aut per majores, &c. Undè sequi videtur, hominem se ipsum discernere, contra Paulum, & in homine esse causam dispositivam ad gratiam, vel dispositiones prævias ad fidem, contrà Lutheri constantem doctrinam, in Libris De Servo Arbitrio, De Origine Fidei, & Præfat. in Epist. ad Romanos, &c.
